physical_harm: The deceased sustained 8 injuries, 4 of which were grievous, and P.W. 3 sustained injuries which were confirmed by medical examination.
number_of_offences: Offences under Sections 147, 148, 149, 302 and 294 IPC were charged; conviction under Section 302 read with Sections 148 and 149 IPC was upheld.
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation as the accused were armed and made a pronouncement that the deceased could not escape that day.
motive: Old enmity, as indicated in the Crime Details Form.
key_evidence_accepted: The court accepted the evidence of the two eye-witnesses, which was fully corroborated by other witnesses, and the version of the eye-witnesses was supported by other circumstances of the case.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that the evidence of P.W.3 as an eye-witness was cogent in every respect and fully supported by the version of P.W.6 and corroborated by the evidence of P.Ws. 7 and 11.

legal_representation.accused: Tripurari Ray, Dhirendra Singh Parmar, Suresh Kumar Sharma, Rajinder Singh, Susheel Tomar, Ms. Abha R. Sharma, B Advs.
legal_representation.state: Arjun Garg, Manish Yadav, Mishra Saurabh, Advs.

investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the FIR was registered at 10:45 p.m. on 27th June, 1997, and that the evidence of the eye-witnesses was fully corroborated by other witnesses, establishing the occurrence as deposed by the eye-witnesses and the involvement of the appellants.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the FIR was ante-dated, the injuries sustained by P.W. 3 were fake, and the non-mentioning of P.W. 3 in the Crime Details Form vitiated the prosecution's case, as well as that the delay in forwarding the Express Report caused prejudice to the appellants.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the delay in forwarding the Express Report does not necessarily vitiate the case unless prejudice to the accused is shown, and that the testimony of an injured witness is accorded a special status in law.
precedent_relied_upon: Pala Singh v. State of Punjab (1972) 2 SCC 640; State of Kamataka v. Main Patel (1996) 8 SCC 167; Bhajan Singh @ Harbhajan Singh & Ors. v. State of Haryana (2011) 7 SCC 421
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the occurrence was sufficiently established as spoken to by the eye-witnesses, and the involvement of the appellants was fully established.
